name: lfx-marketing-os
description: Public plugin marketplace for The Linux Foundation's LFX Marketing OS agents and skills.

plugins.name: marketing-plan-workbook-agent
plugins.description: v0.3.0 — Builds the pre-filled Marketing Plan Workbook (.pptx) an ED completes before the planning interview. First Plan mode opens with a 'Where we stand today' LFX baseline when no prior plan exists; goals tie to the four standard business outcomes with KPI, budget share, timeline and risks; budget set by Strategy Profile (12/20/30% of revenue) and split into paid, LF services, third-party content and discretionary reserve; closes with a Goals Summary table and Budget Summary slide. Feeds the final marketing plan agent.

plugins.name: qtrly-marketing-review-agent
plugins.description: Generates a pre-filled Quarterly Marketing Review workbook (.pptx) for a foundation's marketing team at quarter end — goals-vs-actuals scorecard, business outcomes, engine-health conversions, channel indicators, vehicle scorecards, market signals, and a structured insights retrospective, pre-filled from LFX and marketing platform data with DRAFT badges and YOUR INPUT questions. The completed review is an input to marketing-plan-workbook-agent, and its Executive Summary is presented to the ED at the quarterly plan review.

plugins.name: brand-guidelines-agent
plugins.description: Asks first for the foundation's own brand or messaging documents and maps them into the standard fields, pulls the project's LFX record and runs a research sweep, interviews only for the gaps (or pre-fills in batch mode), and generates a short project Brand Kit — a two-page Review Sheet for the ED, then positioning, brand principle, voice and prefer/avoid language, what we don't claim, competitive guardrails, LFX-derived governance and trademark wording, and a five-component visual identity direction — held to a 6–8 page budget, delivered Google Docs-ready on the LF Agent DOCS Template with a structured .fields.yaml sidecar for downstream agents.

plugins.name: message-foundation-agent
plugins.description: Asks first for the foundation's own messaging documents and maps them into the standard fields, interviews only for the gaps (or pre-fills in batch mode), and produces a short '[Project Name] Message Foundation' built on the LF communications framework: a two-page Review Sheet for the ED, then Vision → Mission → Positioning Platform → Tagline, word-count-locked summaries, boilerplate, llms.txt and elevator pitch, 3–6 messaging pillars on a fixed scaffold with the Message Matrix derived from them, sourced proof points only, objections with honest admissions, what we don't claim, and four CTA anchors — held to an 8–10 page budget, with LFX-derived governance wording, a claims lint and a QA gate. Delivered Google Docs-ready on the LF Agent DOCS Template with a structured .fields.yaml sidecar.

plugins.name: icp-target-markets-agent
plugins.description: Asks first for the foundation's own audience, persona or competitive documents and maps them into the standard fields, reads the project's Brand Kit, Message Foundation Doc and GitHub README, pulls live LFX membership data, runs a competitor scan that includes members' like-for-like products, interviews only for the gaps (or pre-fills in batch mode), and produces a short '[Project Name] Target Markets and ICP' document — a two-page Review Sheet for the ED, market segments, firmographics, organization-level ICPs, 4–9 personas on one fixed eleven-field template with 'what NOT to say', persona selection cues and map, Fit × Warmth rules with hand-raiser signals, a run-rate SOM proposal — held to an 8–10 page budget, with a claims lint and a QA gate. Delivered Google Docs-ready on the LF Agent DOCS Template with a structured .fields.yaml sidecar.

plugins.name: audience-lists-agent
plugins.description: v0.1.0 — Builds a project's Audience Lists document from its Brand Kit, Message Foundation and ICP: a tiered, prioritized earned media target list (the strategy deck's five tiers) with strategy and lead message per outlet and the news hooks to use; the top 5–15 social media voices already talking about the project from Octolens and LFX Lens, in three relationship tiers with next actions; and up to 20 existing audiences in HubSpot, Twilio Segment and LFX owned by other foundations with overlapping ICPs, with owner, size, overlapping message and CTA. One Word document on the LF Agent DOCS template re-skinned with the project's brand via lf-output-formatter. Read-only against every system.

plugins.name: lfx-marketing-os-qa
plugins.description: QA gate for the foundation documents and their derivatives: derives legal-entity and trademark wording from the LFX project record, re-runs every Live-LFX figure through the LFX MCP, refreshes published counters, sweeps the project site / GitHub org / LF press archive for material the intake missed, scans for competitors the brief left out, checks superlatives and dates, and applies a brand-review rubric with severity-ranked before/after fixes. Returns PASS / PASS WITH FIXES / FAIL, a ranked fix list with drop-in replacement text, and a two-page digest. Run before a Brand Kit, Message Foundation or ICP document is marked 'for review'.

plugins.name: plain-writing
plugins.description: Writes and revises prose in a plain style: simple words, complete sentences, no dashes, no jargon, no filler. Includes an optional HTML revision view that shows what changed and why.

plugins.name: marketing-committee-chair-recommendation
plugins.description: When no one volunteers to chair an LF project's marketing committee, pulls the committee roster and member tiers from LFX, checks each representative's title and seniority on LinkedIn through the user's Chrome browser, scans social listening for members already talking about the project, and delivers a ranked shortlist (first ask, second ask, vice-chair) with reasons, committee coverage gaps, and a suggested approach — as a Google Doc or Artifact page. Nothing is sent to candidates.

plugins.name: website-designer-agent
plugins.description: Turns an LF project's three foundation docs into an approved sitemap, a complete Hugo website, and a GitHub-deployed, DNS-ready launch package — with four human approval gates.

plugins.name: qtrly-plan-agent
plugins.description: Guides a Linux Foundation ED/Project Leader through the quarterly review cycle (review outcomes vs. goals, set business-outcome direction, define ranked goals with KPIs, budgets, timelines, and risks) and produces a Google Slides-ready quarterly marketing plan deck.

plugins.name: qtrly-campaign-plan-agent
plugins.description: Takes the quarterly marketing plan produced by qtrly-plan-agent (plus the Brand Kit, Message Foundation, ICP & Target Markets, and Pitch Deck) and produces a single Quarterly Campaign Brief (.docx): the set of campaigns supporting each goal, each with a leader, mediums and sources, and per source the target markets, ICP/personas, key messages, assets to be created, CTAs, and message sequences — plus the ordered list of content creation and source execution agents to run. CFT strategy layer only; does not create content or execute channels.

plugins.name: hot-campaign-workbook-agent
plugins.description: IDENTIFY stage of the Hot Campaigns workflow. When an ED or marketing leader flags a trigger (goal off track, industry news, a release, a viral post, a competitor move) or asks the agent to scan for one, it reads the core documents, quarterly plan and campaign brief, results report, Content Plan, social listening and newsfeed, interviews the runner, and produces a pre-filled Hot Campaign Workbook (.pptx): a Hot Campaign Card plus ED INPUT / CFT INPUT questions. Feeds hot-campaign-plan-agent.

plugins.name: board-status-infographic
plugins.description: Produces the one-page State of the Foundation board infographic (print-ready PDF plus HTML) for an LF project or foundation ahead of each board meeting: inception-to-today scorecard, goals vs outcomes from the quarterly marketing plan, member survey figures, risks that need board action, investment areas, and the decisions the board must take tagged DISCUSS / REVIEW / VOTE. Reads the Quarterly Marketing Plan deck and the ED's board pre-read first, then interviews the ED for gaps; adaptive block layout, always exactly one page.

plugins.name: lf-zoom-hubspot-notes-logger
plugins.description: Pulls a team member's Zoom meeting notes for today and yesterday, writes them into the matching HubSpot meeting records, opens follow-up tasks on opportunities, and flags ambiguous matches over Slack for manual review. Built for any Linux Foundation Marketing or Sales team.

plugins.name: linkedin-post-agent
plugins.description: Drafts LinkedIn posts about Linux Foundation and open source ecosystem work in the user's authentic voice. Learns the user's profile and tone once, then turns any piece of content into ready-to-post options.

plugins.name: member-pitch-deck
plugins.description: Member Pitch Deck (v2.0.0): generates the standard first-meeting membership overview deck (max 22 slides) for any Linux Foundation project or foundation — About the LF → Introducing the Foundation → How to join — in the LF membership-overview style (white canvas, project Brand Kit accent and fonts, LF co-brand lockup, card/stat/flow/tier layouts), grounded in the project's Brand Kit, Message Foundation, and ICP documents. Command: lf-member-pitch-deck.

plugins.name: case-study-agent
plugins.description: Converts any source content — a YouTube video, interview transcript, meeting notes, recording, or raw text — into an on-brand Word document for an LF project or foundation. Loads the project's Brand Kit and Message Foundation (web-research fallback) and produces a first-draft case study by default, or a blog post, article, summary, or Q&A on request.

plugins.name: member-benefits-briefing
plugins.description: Builds the LF CEO-style member executive briefing deck — “[Company] and the Linux Foundation” — for any LF member: pulls the member's live LFX footprint (memberships, dues, code contributions, maintainers, event participation, training), merges it with the standing LF and open-source-AI narrative, and produces a PowerPoint styled to the LF executive briefing template.

plugins.name: aeo-geo-analyzer
plugins.description: Analyzes any website's AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) performance — AI crawler access, llms.txt, on-page answerability, structured data, and third-party citation authority — and produces a scored report with prioritized recommendations.

plugins.name: social-listening-report
plugins.description: On-demand social listening reports from LFX Lens data: Voices That Matter (high-reach creators), Campaign Echo (launch/announcement pickup), and Ask-Anything briefings — with Google Doc output for historical tracking.

plugins.name: social-sentiment-monitor
plugins.description: Scheduled social sentiment monitor for any LF project or foundation (v0.1.0): asks which project to watch, how often to run, how many days to look back and who should receive the brief; flags negative posts and unusually high engagement or reach from LFX Lens (Octolens data in Snowflake) plus live Octolens MCP counters where available; drafts replies with a recommended voice (foundation account, Executive Director, technical lead, ambassador); delivers an LF-template Word brief and Slack DMs to named recipients; and sets itself up as a recurring scheduled task.

plugins.name: run-marketing-impact-report
plugins.description: Marketing Dashboard as a Word document with live data: asks which LF project to run against (e.g. CNCF), pulls figures via the LFX connector (required) and HubSpot (optional), and mirrors the dashboard page by page — Summary, Paid, Social, Web, Direct, Defined Campaigns (goals → campaigns → tactics with KPIs), Budget, the five business outcomes, sources. Sections without a connector say 'Data not available, requires [x] connector'.

plugins.name: member-360
plugins.description: Scores each LF project member's engagement across events, speaking, ambassadors, committees, content, and marketing activity; identifies gaps; and recommends the next best action for Marketing, Member Success, or Sales. Outputs a ranked spreadsheet built for quarterly business reviews.

plugins.name: member-marketing-benefits-audit
plugins.description: LFX Marketing OS Member Marketing Benefits Audit Agent — researches a foundation's website (CNCF by default) for a full calendar year of member-published content, verifies each organisation's membership tier, and reports how much of each tier's measurable marketing benefits (blog submissions, online programs, announcements) was used and remains, as a three-tab reconciling .xlsx audit. Complements member-360 with benefit-level depth.

plugins.name: ambassador-content-assignment
plugins.description: Matches a project's ambassadors against the KubeCon (or any LF event) schedule and generates personalized content assignments — video prompts, social copy, hashtags, tags, and posting recommendations — as a tracker spreadsheet, per-ambassador briefs, and outreach drafts. Then tracks who actually posts via LFX Lens social listening and drafts nudges.

plugins.name: committee-health-agent
plugins.description: Monitors committee participation across an LF project, flags inactive or outdated representatives, identifies member companies without an active contact, and drafts follow-up or replacement outreach for review — a committee-health workbook plus a ready-to-approve outreach queue.

plugins.name: community-monitor-agent
plugins.description: Monitors a project's Slack channels and GitHub repositories on a user-defined schedule, surfaces community questions ranked by sentiment and asker value (community activity and member-company standing), and delivers a live report with drafted replies that can be sent to Slack with one click.

plugins.name: marketing-agent-class
plugins.description: Delivers The Linux Foundation's Claude Agent Workshop marketing training as personalized PowerPoint decks, one section at a time, with live student Q&A captured in a companion deck.

plugins.name: lf-output-formatter
plugins.description: Shared output formatter for every LFX Marketing OS agent: builds decks, documents and letters on the three approved Linux Foundation templates (LF 2025 Google Slides template, LF Agent DOCS template, LF Letterhead) and, for foundation-specific documents, re-skins the template with the foundation's Brand Kit (logo, palette, typography, iconography). Bundles the templates, build scripts, a Brand Kit extractor and a render-and-check step.
